Plot regression effects

Source: R/effects.R
plot_effects.Rd

Plots the expected response, \(x^\top\beta\), against one predictor at a time, with a posterior credible band, over the data. Other predictors are held at their mean (numeric) or reference level (factors). The line is the population-level relationship, averaged over the phylogenetic and other kernel effects, as in a mixed model. For maximum-likelihood fits the line is drawn without a band.

Usage

plot_effects(
  fit,
  effect = NULL,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.95),
  points = TRUE,
  n = 100,
  ndraws = 1000,
  plot = TRUE,
  col = "#4F6D8F",
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

A phylogp_fit.

effect

Names of predictors (variables in the formula) to plot. By default every predictor, one panel each.

probs

Lower and upper quantiles of the band.

points

Draw the data? These are the species values, or the rows for fits with several rows per species.

n

Number of grid values for a numeric predictor.

ndraws

Number of posterior draws used.

plot

Draw the plot? If FALSE, only the values are returned.

col

Colour of the line and band.

...

Further graphical parameters passed to graphics::plot().

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with the predictor (effect), its value (value for numeric predictors, level for factors), the posterior median of the expected response (estimate) and the band (lower, upper).

Details

Named differently from brms::conditional_effects() so that both packages can be loaded together.

References

Bürkner P.-C. 2017. Brms: An R package for Bayesian multilevel models using Stan. Journal of Statistical Software. 80:1–28.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- phylo_gp(brain ~ body, d, tree, k_bm() + k_white())
plot_effects(fit)
plot_effects(fit, "body", probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
} # }
